h1: The 8 Best Ice Makers Under $500, From Nugget Countertops to Commercial Machines, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Ice Maker Under $500: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 ice makers under $500, countertop nugget and bullet units plus commercial machines, scored on output, storage and cleaning.
summary: The EUHOMY 44 lb Nugget Ice Maker is the best ice maker under $500 for most homes, producing soft chewable nugget ice at up to 44 lbs a day with self-cleaning. The EUHOMY stainless nugget is the closer-to-budget choice, the VEVOR commercial machine is the pick for parties and small businesses, and the Sweetcrispy is the cheapest way to have bullet ice at home.
intro: Ice makers split into two worlds that share a name: the countertop machine that makes a few pounds an hour and holds a small basket, and the commercial machine that makes ice by the hundred pounds and needs a drain. Under $500 you can buy either, which is where people go wrong. A commercial unit in a studio flat, or a countertop bullet maker for a restaurant, is a mismatch.

These eight machines cover both worlds. They are scored on daily output, ice type, storage, cleaning features and fit for the way you will actually use them. Output figures come from listings, so treat them as best-case numbers under ideal room temperatures.

products.name: EUHOMY Nugget Ice Maker Countertop 44lbs
products.verdict: Up to 44 lbs of soft nugget ice a day with self-cleaning and a scoop and basket.
products.description:
This EUHOMY makes up to 44 lbs of nugget ice per 24 hours, which it markets as sonic ice, the soft, chewable style. It has a self-cleaning cycle and includes an ice scoop and basket, in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Nugget ice is the reason people buy this class: it is chewable, it soaks up drink flavour and it is why fast food chains use it. At 44 lbs a day it produces more than the other nugget units here, which matters in a house that goes through ice at dinner. The cost is a larger body and a fan that runs when the machine makes ice.

Buy it if your household loves chewable ice. Skip it if you want clear, hard cubes for cocktails.

products.name: EUHOMY Nugget Ice Maker Countertop Stainless Steel
products.verdict: A stainless steel nugget maker with 35 lb daily output and a 7 minute cycle.
products.description:
This stainless EUHOMY produces 35 lbs of ice a day on a 7-minute cycle, with a self-cleaning cycle, a scoop and a basket.

Stainless steel resists staining and dents and fits modern kitchens better than plastic. Output is lower than the 44 lb unit, though a 7 minute cycle means a first batch of ice arrives promptly. It ranks second because the extra output of the first pick matters more to heavy ice users than the finish.

Buy it if looks and a good cycle time matter. Skip it if you need maximum ice.
cons: Less output than the 44 lb unit
products.idealFor: Stainless kitchens with moderate ice needs.

products.name: EUHOMY Nugget Ice Maker Countertop with Handle
products.verdict: 34 lbs per day with a 6-minute cycle, a carry handle and a removable top cover.
products.description:
This EUHOMY nugget maker produces 34 lbs per day with a 6-minute cycle, a removable top cover and an auto-clean routine. It includes a basket and scoop and has a carry handle.

The handle makes it easy to move between a kitchen and a patio. It ranks third because output is a notch lower than the stainless unit while the faster cycle partly offsets it. The removable top cover simplifies wiping the inside.

Buy it if you want to carry the machine around. Skip it if output matters most.
products.idealFor: Portable use at parties and patios.

products.name: VEVOR Commercial Ice Maker Machine
products.verdict: 130 lbs a day with 16 to 30 lbs of storage, in built-in, freestanding or under-counter form.
products.description:
The VEVOR is a commercial machine producing 130 lbs per 24 hours with 16 to 30 lbs of storage, a stainless steel body, LED display and self-cleaning. It installs built-in, freestanding or under a counter.

It is the best choice for parties, bars and small shops that run out of countertop ice in an hour. Commercial machines need a water line and a drain, which is installation work a countertop unit avoids. It lands near the top of the budget.

Buy it if you serve a crowd. Skip it if you have no drain.

products.name: Mojgar Commercial Ice Maker Machine
products.verdict: 100 lbs a day with 18 to 33 lbs of storage in a commercial-grade body.
products.description:
The Mojgar produces 100 lbs per 24 hours and stores 18 to 33 lbs, built to a commercial grade.

It sits behind the VEVOR because output is lower and the listing gives fewer details about installation and cleaning. It offers slightly more storage, which helps through a busy evening.

Buy it if you want a commercial machine with more storage. Skip it if you need the highest output.
products.skipIf: You want the highest daily output.

products.name: EUHOMY Ice Maker Countertop with 2 Ice Sizes
products.verdict: 26 lbs a day of bullet ice in 2 sizes, with 9 cubes in 6 minutes.
products.description:
This EUHOMY makes 9 bullet ice cubes in 6 minutes, up to 26 lbs a day, in two cube sizes with self-cleaning, a basket and scoop.

Bullet ice is hard and cloudy, the classic cocktail and water-bottle ice. Two sizes let you pick small cubes for tumblers and larger ones for pitchers. It ranks sixth because nugget machines suit families better, and its output is lower.

Buy it if you want cube-style ice at a lower cost. Skip it if you want chewable ice.

products.name: EUHOMY Countertop Ice Maker with Handle
products.verdict: 26 lbs a day of bullet ice, 9 cubes in 6 minutes, with a carry handle and auto-clean.
products.description:
This black EUHOMY makes up to 26 lbs in 24 hours, 9 cubes per 6 minutes, with auto-cleaning, a basket and scoop, and a carry handle.

It ranks seventh because it overlaps the two-size model, which offers more choice for the same price bracket. The handle is useful for a small kitchen where the machine is stored away.

Buy it if you want to move the machine around. Skip it if you want two cube sizes.
products.idealFor: Occasional ice needs and small kitchens.

products.name: Sweetcrispy Countertop Ice Maker
products.verdict: 26.5 lbs a day in two ice sizes, with a scoop and basket, in the lowest bracket.
products.description:
The Sweetcrispy makes 9 cubes in 6 minutes, up to 26.5 lbs in 24 hours, in 2 ice sizes with a scoop and basket. It is among the cheapest here.

This is the least expensive way to own an ice maker. It ranks last because it lacks the self-cleaning mention of the EUHOMY models and its brand history is shorter.

Buy it if budget is the priority. Skip it if you want a self-cleaning routine.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want ice now.

whatMatters.detail: Nugget ice is soft and chewable, and absorbs flavour. Bullet ice is harder and cloudier, and lasts longer in a drink. Decide which you prefer before looking at output.
A 26 lb machine makes about 1 lb an hour, so a party exhausts it quickly. Commercial units at 100 to 130 lbs serve crowds. Match the figure to your typical peak demand, not an average day.
Countertop machines hold only a small basket of ice, and the rest melts back into the reservoir. Commercial models store 16 to 33 lbs. Storage tells you how long ice lasts between refills.
Standing water breeds mould and slime. A self-cleaning cycle flushes the system, but you still need to wipe and descale. Look for the feature on the listing.
Countertop machines recycle meltwater into a reservoir. Commercial machines need a drain line. Check your plumbing before buying one.

faq.q: Why does my ice maker melt ice?
faq.a: Countertop models keep ice in a basket that is not refrigerated, so it melts and drains back to the reservoir. This is normal. Scoop the ice into a freezer bag for storage.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Ignoring ice type. Nugget and bullet ice suit different drinks. Pick the one you will use before comparing output.

faq.q: Is the nugget maker worth it over a bullet maker?
faq.a: If you love chewable ice, yes. It costs more but is the style many people actually prefer. Bullet makers are cheaper and better for cocktails.

faq.q: How hard is it to set up?
faq.a: Countertop units need only water and an outlet. Commercial units need a water line and a drain, and usually a plumber.
Run the self-cleaning cycle regularly and wipe the basket. Descale monthly with a citric acid solution, following the manual.

faq.q: How much space does it need?
faq.a: Leave several inches around the vents for airflow. Keep it away from heat sources.

finalTake: The EUHOMY Nugget Ice Maker with 44 lbs a day is the best ice maker under $500 for most homes: soft nugget ice, self-cleaning and plenty of output. The stainless EUHOMY is the stylish alternative, and the VEVOR commercial machine suits crowds. The Sweetcrispy is the cheapest cube maker. Decide on ice type and drain access first.
